rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: # Incomplete dominance and codominance ## 1. Introduction Opening frame for **Incomplete dominance and codominance** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Heredity and Evolution fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  Mendel's peas showed **complete dominance**: the heterozygote looks exactly like the dominant parent. Most genes are not that polite. When the heterozygote is intermediate, the inheritance is **incomplete dominance**; when both alleles are fully and separately visible, it is **codominance**. Neither pattern breaks the Law of Segregation — in both, the F₂ genotypic ratio is still 1:2:1.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Incomplete dominance: heterozygote is INTERMEDIATE (red × white snapdragon → pink); F2 = 1:2:1 both genotypic and phenotypic — the ratio change from 3:1 is the mark.  ·  Trick 2: Codominance: BOTH alleles express fully (AB blood group: IA and IB codominant; i is recessive) — no blending, both products appear.

(3) ABO blood group genotypes and transfusion compatibility.…  ·  ## 8. Summary and self-check 5–10 line chapter summary, self-check questions and the common-confusions list (block VIII) — completed in the unit fill pass.  ·  **Summary.** Dominance is a matter of degree. Incomplete dominance dilutes the heterozygote (pink snapdragon), codominance displays both alleles at once (AB blood). Both keep the 1:2:1 genotypic ratio and both make genotype readable from phenotype.…
